beats.story: The "grocery shop of shame" is a form of modern art that peaks in its grandeur at the conveyer belt. My post - aunty dinner angst may have influenced what went into the basket. Plus, the signature sky-blue color painted all over Supershops -- the same shade that brands everything in our office -- triggers something in me that can only be cured by processed foods. All the items that I plan to purchase and consume are splayed out and slowly gliding toward the cashier, a visual representation of the state of my mental health. The weeks when I get the marshmallow strawberries and the Corn Nuts are particular cries for help. The key to a successful grocery shop of shame is all about timing. Eight p.m. on a Monday is usually the safest hour if you want a little discretion, but somehow there are two people behind me tonight.
beats.story_cn: “羞耻杂货铺”堪称现代艺术，而其巅峰展现在那条传送带上。姨妈家晚餐后的焦虑大概影响了购物篮的内容物。加之超市品牌标志性的天蓝色——和我们办公室里那种令人窒息的同款色调——总能触发我某种症状，唯有加工食品方能治愈。此刻所有我计划购买并吞下的食物，正摊开在传送带上缓缓滑向收银台，这简直是对我精神健康状态的视觉解构。特别是那些买了棉花糖草莓和玉米坚果的日子，简直是在大声呼救。经营好这家羞耻杂货铺的关键在于时机。周一晚上八点通常是保持体面的最佳时段，但偏偏今晚我身后就站了两个人。

beats.story: Worst of all, the one closest to me looks to be the juicing type. We wait in meditative silence as the cashier scans the items in hollow beeping intervals. I add the Flamin' Hot Cheetos -- was that a gasp? The guy behind me winces as he eyes my treats, and he looks like he might shit his high-end sweatpants. He clearly doesn't understand my craft. He's perfect and sinewy and could make it as a time-share brochure model if he desired. He glances at his teal Apple Watch, grunts, then lifts his basket of produce from the ground and storms away. If only I could leave this situation too.
beats.story_cn: 最糟糕的是，排在我后面那家伙看起来像个榨汁养生党。我们在冥想般的沉默中等待，收银扫描仪以空洞的哔哔声间隔着扫过商品。我放进火辣奇多——刚才那是一声抽气吗？身后男人盯着我的零食龇牙咧嘴，那表情仿佛要在名牌运动裤里当场失禁。他显然不懂我的哲学。他完美而精瘦，若愿意完全可以去当分时度假广告男模。他瞥了眼蓝绿色苹果手表，咕哝一声，提起地上那篮生鲜怒气冲冲地走了。要是我也能逃离这处境该多好。

beats.story: The guy behind him shuffles forward and grabs the last bag of All- Dressed peanuts I'd been eyeing. My stomach twists as he adds it to his pile. It's him. Him as in Clifford HR guy. He's dressed like a British gangster in an Adidas sweatsuit, and his basket is filled with puffy bags of chips with reckless flavors made for eating alone: pickled onion, chilly and chive. Solidarity. His gaze shifts from the conveyer belt to me. He jolts in surprise, then a genuine smile overtakes him.
beats.story_cn: 他身后那个男人蹭上前，抓走了我盯了半天的最后一包全味花生。看着他把它扔进自己篮子时，我的胃拧成了麻花。是他。就是人事部那个克利福德。他穿着阿迪达斯运动套装，活像英国黑帮片里走出来的角色，篮子里塞满了各种为孤独享用而设计的放纵口味膨化食品：腌洋葱味、辣椒香葱味。真是同类。他目光从传送带移到我身上，惊讶地一怔，随即展露真诚笑容。

beats.story: "Jolene, what the hell? So good to see you." "Nice to see another patron of the arts." I look pointedly at his snacks, and his grin tugs a little wider. Only it's too much -- what is he doing here, after everything today? Maybe Supershops hired him to monitor me at all company locations. Maybe this is a social experiment on how to break a person in one day. "You're doing a good job acting surprised," I say. "What?" He raises a brow, but he's still smiling. He's a stark contrast to the scuffed floors and depressive Supershops-branded endcaps.
beats.story_cn: “乔琳，搞什么鬼？见到你太好了。”“真高兴碰到另一位艺术鉴赏家。”我刻意扫视他的零食，他的笑容又咧开些许。但这笑容太过分了——经历了今天种种之后他究竟为何会出现在这里？也许超市雇佣他来监视我在所有公司门店的举动。也许这是一场关于如何在一天内摧毁一个人的社会实验。“你装得很惊讶嘛。”我说。“什么？”他挑起眉毛，但笑意未减。他站在磨损的地板和令人沮丧的超市品牌端头架前，形成鲜明反差。

beats.story: "Are you saying this isn't some kind of HR undercover op then? Gregory isn't hiding in the store, dicking up the produce with his fingers as we speak?" He lets out a startled chuckle. "What did you just say?" I should probably be embarrassed that I said that out loud. But running into him here is the cherry on top of my surreal day. This feels like a glitch in the matrix or a dream. So I poke some more. "I'm off work. This is my time; I can say 'peen-hole' if I want." I stare him down like this is a dare.
beats.story_cn: “所以你不是在说这是什么人力资源部的卧底行动对吧？格雷戈里此刻没躲在店里用手指戳弄生鲜吧？”他噗嗤笑出声。“你刚说什么？”我本该为自己脱口而出的话感到窘迫。但在这里撞见他，反倒成了我这超现实一天的顶上樱桃。这感觉像是矩阵故障，或是场梦境。于是我继续撩拨。“我下班了，这是我的私人时间，想说‘命根子’也随我。”我迎着他的目光，仿佛这是一场挑衅。

beats.story: After all, he spent my performance meeting doodling cats, so he's not the paradigm of professionalism either. "That's fifty-six seventy-three," the cashier chimes in neutrally. I tap the machine to pay and thank her, but I keep my eyes on Cliff. His brow crinkles. "I was referring to the part about Gregory. I would never bring him on an undercover operation. He doesn't have what it takes." I try not to laugh in surprise, but it feels like he passed some kind of test. To hide my amusement, I narrow my eyes at his groceries.
beats.story_cn: 毕竟他在我绩效评估会上画猫玩，所以他自己也不是什么专业典范。“五十六块七三，”收银员平淡地报数。我轻点机器付款并向她道谢，但目光始终锁着克里夫。他眉头皱起。“我说的是关于格雷戈里的部分。我绝不会带他执行卧底任务，他不够格。”我强忍住惊讶的笑意，这感觉像是通过了某种测试。为掩饰笑意，我眯眼打量起他的购物清单。

beats.story: His eyes follow my gaze. "As you can see, I'm just here for my essentials." He nods toward the front entrance. "I just live a few blocks away." I take a step back. "So do I. I shop here all the time for our employee discount. I've never seen you before." "Well, you wouldn't have recognized me. We only met a few days ago." "I suppose." I nod politely to the cashier as she hands me my receipt. "Well, bye," I mutter as I grab the frayed handles of my Supershops reusable bags and hope for peace.
beats.story_cn: 他的目光随我扫视。“如你所见，我只是来买些必需品。”他朝前门方向点头。“我就住附近几个街区。”我后退半步。“我也是，常来这儿用员工折扣买东西。可从没见过你。”“嗯，你当然认不出我，我们几天前才第一次见面。”“大概吧。”收银员递来小票时我礼貌颔首。“那，再见，”我嘟囔着抓起超市环保袋磨得起毛的提手，只盼能清净会儿。

beats.story: "See ya," he calls, and holds up his keys in a wave. I'm already walking through the automatic doors, too far gone to wave back. I trot across the asphalt parking lot with slightly heavier than planned shopping bags. The sun has gone down and things are turning shadowy. The creaky squeal of a retirement-aged car trying its darnedest sounds too close behind me. I turn sharply to face a golden sedan that could be considered vintage if the world didn't want to forget this model ever existed. "You're not walking home with that many groceries, are you?" Cliff calls from his rolled-down passenger-side window. I shrug as best as I can with the pounds of sugar weighing them down.
beats.story_cn: “回见！”他喊道，晃了晃手里的钥匙。我早已穿过自动门，远得无法挥手回应。拎着沉甸甸的购物袋快步走过沥青停车场，太阳下山后周遭渐渐暗下。身后传来老款汽车竭力启动的吱呀声，近得令人心惊。我猛地转身，正对一辆金色轿车——若非世人巴不得遗忘这个车型的存在，它或许能被称作古董。“你该不会要拎着这么多杂货走回家吧？”克里夫摇下车窗喊道。我肩头被几公斤白糖压得生疼，仍尽量耸了耸肩。

beats.story: "It's how I keep my fitness levels optimum." Although, if we're being honest, the Alphagetti cans were a poor choice. "I'll give you a ride," he says, without hesitation. "Nah, we're good," I say back, also without hesitation. "You sure you're okay walking home in the dark?" As if on cue, the streetlamp above me flickers on, casting a creepy fluorescent sheen over the tar lot. Cliff stretches himself over the passenger seat and opens the side door. "Come on, it's no trouble." He nods toward my grocery bags. "Anyone can see your spicy Cheetos; you're going to get mugged." For the second time this evening, I find myself biting back a smile. I stare at the sidewalk ahead.

beats.story: Admittedly the neighborhood has been on the sketchier side after dark these days. But would getting mugged be as bad as him seeing where I live? The interior light in his car clicks on, like a moth lamp beckoning me in, so I accept my fate. "Just so you know, I've been doing this route for eight years sans incident," I say as I unload my bags into the passenger-side footwell. The tang of relief in my forearms is almost too much. "But thanks." The interior of the car smells about how you'd imagine. There's a New Car Smell air freshener hanging on the rearview mirror that must be ironic, because I'm picking up old-dog vibes. Music is quietly filtering through the crackly speakers, but it's instrumental and low and sends a soothing warmth into my chest.
beats.story_cn: 平心而论，这片街区近来入夜后确实愈发不太平。但被抢劫真比让他看见我住处更糟？车内顶灯咔哒亮起，像诱蛾灯般召唤着我，我索性认命上车。“提前声明，我走这条路八年从未出事。”我边说边把购物袋堆到副驾驶脚边。小臂肌肉松弛的释然感几乎令人晕眩。“但还是谢谢你。”车内气味如你想象般复杂。后视镜悬着“新车清香”香氛片，讽刺意味明显——我嗅到的是老派绅士的温厚气息。音响流淌出低回器乐，沙哑扬声器滤出的暖调旋律渗入胸腔。

I nod and brace for his impending judgment. I'm not sure how many more knocks I can take today. This time I can't catch it fast enough -- a chuckle escapes me. "I didn't think you had it in you to make a decent joke." "Hey, I'm off the clock too." His right arm is resting on the center console, and I swear I can feel the warmth of it radiating through the car's interior.

beats.story_cn: “他们还在搞那种公开展览会吗？”我忍俊不禁，笑声尖锐刺耳。这家伙今晚怎么连续两次让我破功？趁他盯着路面，我大胆地多凝视了几秒，仿佛他的脸能泄露脑中所想。“平心而论，那场表演确实物超所值。”我俏皮回击。“但说真的，没事的。我猜我们这种小员工本来就没资格跟HR拼车吧。”“信不信由你，管理层规定企业机器人可以与员工友好相处。只是不能谈恋爱。”他双手紧握方向盘，目光扫向后视镜。“抱歉，我不是指——这不是个——”“老天，绝对不是。”我打断道。

beats.story: His knuckles loosen. "You flatter." But then his eyes soften. "Totally don't want to make things awkward, though. The offer's there, but no pressure. I get it could be weird." He obviously offered only out of obligation because of my weird comment about his parking spot, but I can't carpool with a corporate cop, anyway -- no matter how much he wants to act otherwise. Besides, if we commuted together, he'd just ask tons of questions, and we'd get to know more and more useless shit about each other, and then we'd get to the useful parts and . . .
beats.story_cn: 他指节微微放松。“你过奖了。”但眼神却柔和下来。“不过完全不想让事情变得尴尬。提议在这，但没压力。我知道可能有点怪。”他显然只是因为我那句关于停车位的怪话才尽义务般提出，而且我无论如何不能跟企业警察拼车——就算他表现得再随和也不行。再说了，如果一起通勤，他肯定会问一堆问题，我们会渐渐了解彼此越来越多鸡毛蒜皮的事，然后触及那些有分量的隐私，接着……

beats.story: I shake that train of thought away. "Thanks, I appreciate it, but I'm good." Yes, it's only because he's HR that we can't carpool. He pulls up to the curb of my street -- or, I guess, our street now -- soundless but for the clicking of the turn signal. I hold my breath as my building comes into view, with its broken sign and the empty shopping cart leaning sideways on the front lawn. Those things were invisible to me just yesterday. Why did I have to tell him where I live? This is too much. What if I leave the hall light on, the one I always forget about, and he sees my colossal dish pile through the window?
beats.story_cn: 我甩开那纷乱的思绪。“谢了，不用麻烦——我自己能行。”是了，正因为他做人事，我们才不能拼车。他将车悄无声息地滑到我住的街边——或者该说，如今是我们住的街边——只有转向灯在哒哒作响。我的公寓楼映入眼帘：歪斜的招牌，前院草坪上侧倒着的空购物车。昨天这些景象还仿佛不存在。我何必告诉他我家地址？这太过分了。要是我忘了关客厅那盏总忘关的灯，他透过窗户看到我堆积如山的脏碗盘怎么办？

beats.story: What if he deems my apartment unsafe for human life and has to make a report to headquarters about me? What if Miley's there and she tells him about my tarot reading? He can track my comings and goings if he wants to, can inspect my garbage if he so desires. All the calm vibes have dissipated. My seat belt pulls tighter across my chest. I rush to unclip it and open the door. "See you tomorrow." "Hey, I'll help with your -- " I grab the grocery bags in a rapid swoop and slam the door shut before I can hear him finish. It's just that HR people aren't our friends. Nothing else.
beats.story_cn: 万一他认定我的公寓不适合人类居住，非得向总部提交关于我的报告怎么办？万一麦莉在家，跟他讲起我的塔罗牌占卜怎么办？他若愿意，完全可以追踪我的行踪，甚至检查我的垃圾。所有平静的氛围都消散了。安全带勒得我胸口发紧。我慌忙解开它，推开车门。“明天见。”“嘿，我帮你拿——”我飞速抓起购物袋，在他话音落下前砰地关上了车门。只是因为，人事部门的人不是我们的朋友。仅此而已。
